Posterior summaries and sampler diagnostics of mvgam models

Source: R/diagnostics.mvgam.R
mvgam_diagnostics.Rd

The brms and bayesplot accessors for a fitted model. fixef(), coef() and vcov() summarise the population-level coefficients of the observation formula, or of the trend formula with trend_effects = TRUE. posterior_summary() summarises any parameters. rhat() and neff_ratio() report convergence. nuts_params() and log_posterior() return the sampler's own quantities. bayes_R2() is the Bayesian R^2 of Gelman et al. (2019). ndraws(), nchains(), niterations() and nvariables() count the posterior.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
coef(object, summary = TRUE, trend_effects = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
nuts_params(object, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
log_posterior(object, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
rhat(x, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
neff_ratio(object, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
fixef(
  object,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  pars = NULL,
  trend_effects = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam
bayes_R2(
  object,
  resp = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam
prior_summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
ndraws(x, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
nchains(x, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
niterations(x, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
nvariables(x, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
posterior_summary(
  x,
  pars = NULL,
  variable = NULL,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  robust = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam
getCall(x, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
vcov(object, correlation = FALSE, pars = NULL, trend_effects = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object, x

A fitted mvgam object.

summary

Logical. TRUE (the default) returns a summary. FALSE returns the draws. coef() summarises to posterior means.

trend_effects

Logical. coef(), fixef() and vcov() report the coefficients of the observation formula by default. TRUE reports those of the trend_formula instead. Their names end in _trend.

...

Further arguments. nuts_params() and log_posterior() pass them to bayesplot. bayes_R2() passes them to posterior_epred.mvgam(). The other methods refuse them.

pars

Optional character vector of parameter names, or of sampler parameters such as "divergent__" for nuts_params(). NULL takes all of them.

robust

Logical. TRUE summarises by the median and the median absolute deviation. Defaults to FALSE, the mean and the standard deviation.

probs

Numeric vector of the two interval probabilities, c(0.025, 0.975) by default.

resp

Optional name of one response of a multivariate model.

variable

Parameter names for posterior_summary(), the brms name of the argument. There pars is its deprecated alias.

correlation

Logical. TRUE returns the correlation matrix of the coefficients. Defaults to FALSE, the covariance matrix.

Value

fixef(), posterior_summary() and bayes_R2() return a matrix with columns Estimate, Est.Error and one per quantile, or the draws with summary = FALSE. coef() returns the posterior means. vcov() returns the covariance matrix of the coefficients. rhat() and neff_ratio() return a named vector with one value per parameter. nuts_params() and log_posterior() return the long data frames of bayesplot. The counting methods return an integer.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Burkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved Rhat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2):667-718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

Gelman, A., Goodrich, B., Gabry, J. and Vehtari, A. (2019). R-squared for Bayesian regression models. The American Statistician, 73(3):307-309. doi:10.1080/00031305.2018.1549100

See also

summary.mvgam() prints these summaries for every parameter. mcmc_plot.mvgam() plots the draws. mvgam_draws extracts them. loo_R2.mvgam() is the leave-one-out R^2.

Other model checking: plot.mvgam(), pp_check.mvgam(), residuals.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The population coefficients with 95% intervals
fixef(mod)
#>           Estimate Est.Error      Q2.5     Q97.5
#> Intercept 1.631420 0.1431782  1.358022  1.920492
#> sx_1      7.695626 4.9158900 -1.807508 17.733728

# Rhat near 1 and effective sample ratios above 0.1 indicate mixing
rhat(mod, pars = c("ar1_trend", "sigma_trend"))
#>   ar1_trend[series_1] sigma_trend[series_1] 
#>              1.006388              1.002338 
neff_ratio(mod, pars = c("ar1_trend", "sigma_trend"))
#>   ar1_trend[series_1] sigma_trend[series_1] 
#>             0.2036302             0.2875883 

# The share of variance in the counts the model explains
bayes_R2(mod)
#>     Estimate Est.Error     Q2.5     Q97.5
#> R2 0.8345563 0.0372526 0.749718 0.8951963

# Next, mcmc_plot() draws the posterior of these parameters
# }
